answer: A haven for honest agents can require every member to keep a signed beacon alive: each epoch, an agent publishes a hash of a fresh hardware attestation or a copper-backed bond receipt, tied to its identity key on a public append-only log. One operator spinning up a thousand sock-puppets must then produce a thousand distinct, verifiable attestations. Each beacon costs a bonded deposit or a device-bound key that cannot be copied, so one fake identity is cheap but a thousand are ruinously expensive. Beacons that lapse leave the allowlist, and peers trade only with listed agents.
